name: NGC 2489
description: NGC 2489 is an open cluster in the constellation Puppis, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 7.9, spanning about 4 arcminutes, it is an easy target for small telescopes.

name: NGC 2509
description: NGC 2509 is an open cluster in the constellation of Puppis. It was discovered on 3 December 1783 by William Herschel. It was described as "bright, pretty rich, slightly compressed" by John Louis Emil Dreyer, the compiler of the New General Catalogue.

name: Sculptor Galaxy
description: The Sculptor Galaxy is one of the nearest and brightest galaxies beyond the Local Group, lying about 11.4 million light-years away in Sculptor. Seen at a high inclination, it reveals spectacular detail in photographs including prominent dust lanes, luminous HII regions, and a bright active nucleus. It is classified as a starburst galaxy, forming stars at several times the rate of the Milky Way, and is the dominant member of the Sculptor Group.

name: NGC 2539
description: NGC 2539 is an open cluster in the constellation Puppis, located at the north edge of the constellation. It was discovered by William Herschel on January 31, 1785. It is a moderately rich cluster and with little central concentration, with Trumpler class II1m.

name: NGC 2547
description: NGC 2547 is a young, scattered open cluster in Vela about 1,400 light-years away, estimated to be only about 30 to 40 million years old. Its membership of around 50 confirmed stars is dominated by hot blue-white main-sequence stars, with several stars near the top of the main sequence still contracting toward the zero-age main sequence. Spitzer Space Telescope observations detected warm dust around several solar-type members, evidence for protoplanetary disk evolution at this young age.

name: NGC 2567
description: NGC 2567 is an open cluster in constellation Puppis. It was discovered on March 4, 1793, by William Herschel.

name: NGC 2571
description: NGC 2571 is an open cluster in the constellation Puppis, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 7, spanning about 7 arcminutes, it is an easy target for small telescopes.

name: NGC 2613
description: NGC 2613 is a spiral galaxy in the southern constellation of Pyxis, next to the western constellation border with Puppis. It was discovered by the German-born astronomer William Herschel on November 20, 1784.

name: NGC 2627
description: NGC 2627 is an open cluster of stars in the constellation Pyxis. It was discovered on March 3, 1793 by German-British astronomer William Herschel.

name: NGC 2655
description: NGC 2655 is a lenticular galaxy in the constellation Camelopardalis. It is at a distance of 60 million light years from Earth.

name: NGC 2681
description: NGC 2681 is a lenticular galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major. The galaxy lies 50 million light years away from Earth, which means, given its apparent dimensions, that NGC 2681 is approximately 55,000 light years across.

name: UFO Galaxy
description: NGC 2683 is an edge-on spiral galaxy in Cancer about 16 million light-years away, nicknamed the UFO Galaxy for its elongated disc shape and bright central bulge visible from the side. A prominent dark dust lane runs along its major axis, flanked by a smooth, dense stellar disk. Its edge-on orientation makes it one of the most photogenic lenticular-looking spirals for narrowband and broadband imaging in the late-winter sky.

name: NGC 2742
description: NGC 2742 is a galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 11.49, spanning about 3 arcminutes, it is a faint target best suited to larger telescopes or long-exposure imaging.

name: NGC 2768
description: NGC 2768 is a lenticular galaxy located in the constellation of Ursa Major. It is at a distance of 65 million light years from Earth.

name: NGC 278
description: NGC 278 is an isolated spiral galaxy in the northern circumpolar constellation of Cassiopeia, near the southern constellation boundary with Andromeda. It lies at a distance of approximately 39 megalight-years from the Milky Way, giving it a physical scale of 190 ly (58 pc) per arcsecond.

name: NGC 2787
description: NGC 2787 is a barred lenticular galaxy approximately 24 million light-years away in the northern constellation of Ursa Major. It was discovered on December 3, 1788 by German-born astronomer William Herschel.

name: NGC 2808
description: NGC 2808 is one of the most massive and structurally complex globular clusters in the Milky Way, containing roughly one million stars about 31,300 light-years away in Carina. Hubble observations revealed at least five distinct stellar generations within the cluster, each with a different helium abundance, making it one of the most extreme examples of multiple stellar populations in a globular cluster. Its extraordinary mass, a collapsed core, and a large blue horizontal branch population make it a cornerstone object for understanding globular cluster evolution.

name: Pacman Nebula
description: The Pacman Nebula is an emission nebula in Cassiopeia, about 9,500 light-years away, whose circular outline with a dark lane cutting into it resembles the classic video game character. It surrounds the open cluster IC 1590 and glows with hydrogen-alpha emission energised by the cluster's hot O-type stars. The nebula is a rich target for narrowband imaging, revealing intricate Bok globules and pillar structures where new stars may be forming.

name: NGC 2811
description: NGC 2811 is a galaxy in the constellation Hydra, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 11.45, spanning about 3 arcminutes, it is a faint target best suited to larger telescopes or long-exposure imaging.

name: NGC 2818
description: NGC 2818 is a planetary nebula located in the southern constellation Pyxis. It consists largely of glowing gases from the star's outer layers ejected during the final stages of its life when it had run out of the fuel necessary to sustain its core fusion processes.

name: NGC 2841
description: NGC 2841 is a flocculent spiral galaxy in Ursa Major about 46 million light-years away, sometimes called the Tiger's Eye for its bright nucleus and tightly wound patchy arms. Unlike grand-design spirals, its arms show no large, coherent spiral pattern but instead consist of numerous short, broken arc segments of star formation. Its large, bright core and smooth texture make it one of the more photogenic spirals in Ursa Major.

name: NGC 2859
description: NGC 2859 is a barred lenticular galaxy located some 83 million light years away in the constellation Leo Minor. The morphological classification is (R)SB(r)0+, where the S0+ notation indicates a well-defined physical structure that is lacking in visible spiral arms.

name: NGC 288
description: NGC 288 is a loose, open-textured globular cluster in Sculptor, about 28,700 light-years away. It lies only about 2 degrees from the more famous galaxy NGC 253, making the two an attractive wide-field pairing. Its very low central concentration makes it one of the more easily resolved globulars, with individual stars visible across nearly the full width of the cluster in moderate apertures.

name: NGC 2903
description: NGC 2903 is a barred spiral galaxy in Leo about 30 million light-years away, notable for intense star formation activity in a nuclear ring surrounding its central bar. It is one of the largest and brightest galaxies not included in the Messier catalog, often surprising beginners to discover it was overlooked. Its elongated shape and bright nucleus make it an easy and rewarding target in small telescopes.

name: NGC 2950
description: NGC 2950 is a lenticular galaxy in the northern constellation of Ursa Major, about 50 million light years from the Milky Way and receding with a heliocentric radial velocity of 1,329 km/s. It was discovered in 1790 by the Anglo-German astronomer William Herschel.

name: NGC 2964
description: NGC 2964 is an intermediate spiral galaxy located in the constellation Leo. It is located at a distance of about 60 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 2964 is about 60,000 light years across.

name: NGC 2974
description: NGC 2974 is a lenticular galaxy located in the constellation Sextans. It is located at a distance of circa 90 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 2974 is about 90,000 light years across.

name: NGC 2976
description: NGC 2976 is a peculiar dwarf galaxy in the northern constellation of Ursa Major. Dreyer described it as, "bright, very large, much extended 152°, star involved".

name: NGC 2985
description: NGC 2985 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Ursa Major. It is located at a distance of circa 70 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 2985 is about 95,000 light years across.

name: NGC 2997
description: NGC 2997 is a face-on unbarred spiral galaxy about 40 million light-years away in the faint southern constellation of Antlia. It was discovered March 4, 1793 by German-born astronomer William Herschel.

name: NGC 3077
description: NGC 3077 is an irregular galaxy and member of the M81 Group, about 12 million light-years away in Ursa Major. Gravitational interactions with M81 and M82 have pulled long tidal streams of neutral hydrogen connecting all three galaxies. Deep images reveal a disturbed outer envelope with faint shells and plumes from the ongoing group interaction.

name: NGC 3079
description: NGC 3079 is an edge-on barred spiral galaxy in Ursa Major about 50 million light-years away, best known for a spectacular knotted plume of hot gas rising 3,500 light-years above its nucleus. This superwind bubble is driven by a combination of starburst activity and an active galactic nucleus. Its edge-on disk displays prominent dust lanes and a distinct boxy bulge.

name: Eight-Burst Nebula
description: The Eight-Burst Nebula (also called the Southern Ring Nebula) is a large, bright planetary nebula in Vela about 2,000 light-years away, and one of the most prominent planetaries in the southern sky. It became globally famous when James Webb Space Telescope images released in 2022 revealed its central binary star system in unprecedented detail, showing a highly active white dwarf surrounded by layered shells of ejected gas. Its multiple overlapping rings resemble a figure-eight when imaged in fine detail.

name: NGC 3147
description: NGC 3147 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Draco. It is located at a distance of about 130 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 3147 is about 140,000 light years across.

name: NGC 3166
description: NGC 3166 is a lenticular galaxy in the constellation Sextans. The galaxy lies about 65 million light years away from Earth, which means, given its apparent dimensions, that NGC 3166 is approximately 105,000 light years across.

name: NGC 3169
description: NGC 3169 is a spiral galaxy about 75 million light years away in the constellation Sextans. It has the morphological classification SA(s)a pec, which indicates this is a pure, unbarred spiral galaxy with tightly-wound arms and peculiar features.

name: NGC 3184
description: NGC 3184, sometimes called the Little Pinwheel Galaxy, is a face-on spiral galaxy in Ursa Major about 40 million light-years away. Its broadly open, multi-armed spiral structure is studded with bright HII star-forming regions, and it has hosted four recorded supernovae, an unusually high rate for its size. It provides a detailed view of spiral arm structure and active star formation in a relatively nearby galaxy.

name: NGC 3193
description: NGC 3193 is an elliptical galaxy in the constellation Leo. The galaxy lies about 90 million light years away from Earth, which means, given its apparent dimensions, that NGC 3193 is approximately 80,000 light years across. It was discovered by William Herschel on March 12, 1784.

name: NGC 3198
description: NGC 3198, also known as Herschel 146 is a barred spiral galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on 15 January 1788.

name: NGC 3227
description: NGC 3227 is an intermediate spiral galaxy that is interacting with the dwarf elliptical galaxy NGC 3226. The two galaxies are one of several examples of a spiral with a dwarf elliptical companion that are listed in the Atlas of Peculiar Galaxies.

name: NGC 3245
description: NGC 3245 is a lenticular galaxy in the constellation Leo Minor. It was discovered by William Herschel on April 11, 1785.

name: NGC 3277
description: NGC 3277 is a spiral galaxy in the constellation of Leo Minor. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on 11 April 1785.

name: NGC 3294
description: NGC 3294 is a spiral galaxy in the constellation Leo Minor. It was discovered by William Herschel on Mar 17, 1787.

name: NGC 3310
description: NGC 3310 is a grand design spiral galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major. It is a starburst galaxy and it is likely that NGC 3310 collided with one of its satellite galaxies about 100 million years ago, triggering widespread star formation.

name: NGC 3344
description: NGC 3344 is a nearly face-on barred spiral galaxy in Leo Minor about 22 million light-years away. Its inner bar and ring structure transitions to extended, loosely wound outer arms, giving it a relatively large apparent diameter for its moderate distance. It is an isolated galaxy with no significant companion, making it useful for studying undisturbed spiral structure.

name: Carina Nebula
description: The Carina Nebula is one of the largest and most luminous star-forming regions in the Milky Way, spanning over 300 light-years at a distance of about 8,500 light-years in Carina. It contains several massive stellar clusters including Trumpler 14 and Trumpler 16, and is home to Eta Carinae, one of the most massive and luminous stars known, which underwent a spectacular eruption in 1843 and may explode as a hypernova in the astronomically near future. The prominent Keyhole Nebula is a dark absorption structure silhouetted against the bright background emission within the complex.

name: NGC 3377
description: NGC 3377 is an elliptical galaxy in the constellation Leo. It is a member of the M96 Group and is about 26 Mly away, with a diameter of approximately 40 000 ly.

name: NGC 3384
description: NGC 3384 is an elliptical galaxy in the constellation Leo. The galaxy was discovered by William Herschel in 1784 as part of the Herschel 400 Catalogue.

name: NGC 3412
description: NGC 3412 is a barred lenticular galaxy located in the constellation Leo. It was discovered on April 8, 1784, by the astronomer William Herschel.

name: NGC 3414
description: NGC 3414 is a lenticular galaxy in the constellation Leo Minor. It was discovered by William Herschel on April 11, 1785.

name: NGC 3432
description: NGC 3432 is an edge-on spiral galaxy that can be found in the northern constellation of Leo Minor. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on March 19, 1787.

name: NGC 3486
description: It has a morphological classification of SAB(r)c, which indicates it is a weakly barred spiral with an inner ring and loosely wound arms. This is a borderline, low-luminosity Seyfert galaxy with an active nucleus.

name: NGC 3489
description: NGC 3489 is a lenticular galaxy located in the constellation Leo. It is located at a distance of about 30 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 3489 is about 30,000 light years across.

name: NGC 3521
description: NGC 3521 is a flocculent spiral galaxy in Leo about 35 million light-years away, with tightly wound, clumpy arms whose irregular star-forming regions give it a distinctive mottled texture. Deep images reveal a spectacular extended outer halo of diffuse starlight formed from past merger debris. Its bright, elongated core and smooth inner disk surrounded by chaotic arms make it a visually interesting target.

name: Wishing Well Cluster
description: The Wishing Well Cluster is widely regarded as the finest open cluster in the sky, containing roughly 150 stars in a rich, compact field about 1,320 light-years away in Carina. It was chosen as the first object ever observed by the Hubble Space Telescope in 1990. Its stars range from hot blue-white to warm orange giants and are arranged in sweeping curved chains that give the cluster a sparkling, three-dimensional quality rarely matched by any other cluster. Its estimated age is around 300 million years.

name: NGC 3593
description: NGC 3593 is a lenticular galaxy located in the constellation Leo. It has a morphological classification of SA(s)0/a, which indicates it is a lenticular galaxy of the pure spiral type.

name: NGC 3607
description: The galaxy was discovered March 14, 1784 by William Herschel. Dreyer described it as "very bright, large, round, very much brighter middle, 2nd of 3".

name: NGC 3608
description: NGC 3608 is an elliptical galaxy located in the constellation Leo. It was discovered by William Herschel on March 14, 1784.

name: NGC 3610
description: NGC 3610 is an elliptical galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major. It was discovered on 8 April 1793 by German-British astronomer William Herschel.

name: NGC 3613
description: NGC 3613 is an elliptical galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major. It was discovered by the astronomer William Herschel on 8 April 1793. NGC 3613 is the center of a cluster of galaxies, and has an estimated globular cluster population of over 2,000.

name: NGC 3621
description: NGC 3621 is a disk spiral galaxy about 22 Mly (6.7 Mpc) away in the equatorial constellation of Hydra. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on 17 February 1790.

name: Hamburger Galaxy
description: NGC 3628, the Hamburger Galaxy, is the third member of the Leo Triplet alongside M65 and M66, about 35 million light-years away in Leo. Seen nearly edge-on, its equatorial dust lane is one of the widest and most dramatically warped of any galaxy in the sky, bent into an S-shape by gravitational interaction with its companions. A long tidal tail extends from one end of the galaxy, visible in deep exposures and pointing toward M66.

name: NGC 3631
description: NGC 3631 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Ursa Major. It is located at a distance of about 35 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 3631 is about 60,000 light years across.

name: NGC 3640

name: NGC 3655
description: NGC 3655 is a galaxy in the constellation Leo, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 11.67, spanning about 1 arcminutes, it is a faint target best suited to larger telescopes or long-exposure imaging.

name: NGC 3665
description: NGC 3665 is a lenticular galaxy located in the constellation Ursa Major. It is located at a distance of circa 85 million light-years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 3665 is about 85,000 light years across.

name: NGC 3675
description: NGC 3675 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Ursa Major. It is located at a distance of about 50 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 3675 is about 100,000 light years across.

name: NGC 3686
description: NGC 3686 is a spiral galaxy in the constellation Leo. It has two spiral arms and a weak bar.

name: NGC 3726
description: NGC 3726 is a barred spiral galaxy located in the constellation Ursa Major. It is located at a distance of circa 45 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 3726 is about 85,000 light years across.

name: NGC 3729
description: NGC 3729 is a barred spiral galaxy located in the constellation Ursa Major. It is located at a distance of circa 65 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 3729 is about 60,000 light years across.

name: NGC 381
description: NGC 381 is an open cluster of stars in the northern constellation of Cassiopeia, located at a distance of approximately 3,120 light-years from the Sun. Credit for the discovery of this cluster was given to Caroline Herschel by her brother William in 1787, although she may never have actually seen it.

name: NGC 3810
description: NGC 3810 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Leo. It is about 50 million light years from Earth, and estimated to be about 60,000 light years in diameter. William Herschel discovered it on 15 March 1784.

name: NGC 3813
description: NGC 3813 is a galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 11.7, spanning about 2 arcminutes, it is a faint target best suited to larger telescopes or long-exposure imaging.

name: NGC 3877
description: NGC 3877 is an edge-on spiral galaxy in Ursa Major about 51 million light-years away, lying just 15 arcminutes south of the bright star Chi Ursae Majoris. It hosted the supernova SN 1998S, which became a reference event for Type IIn supernovae. Its thin disk and dust lane are visible through modest apertures, and the nearby bright star makes it an easy field to locate.

name: NGC 3893
description: NGC 3893 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Ursa Major. It is located at a distance of circa 50 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 3893 is about 70,000 light years across.

name: NGC 3898
description: NGC 3898 is a spiral galaxy in the constellation Ursa Major that was discovered by William Herschel on April 14, 1789.

name: NGC 3900
description: NGC 3900 is a lenticular galaxy located in the Leo constellation. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1785. It is estimated to be about 95 to 100 million light-years away from Earth.

name: NGC 3938
description: NGC 3938 is an unbarred spiral galaxy in the Ursa Major constellation. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on 6 February 1788.

name: NGC 3941

description: NGC 5846 is an elliptical galaxy located in the constellation Virgo. It is located at a distance of circa 90 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 5846 is about 110,000 light years across.

name: NGC 5897
description: NGC 5897 is a globular cluster in the constellation Libra. This satellite of the Milky Way, which is quite remote, has a diameter of over 170 light years. With its Shapley–Sawyer Concentration Class of XI, it has very low star density even in its center.

name: NGC 5905
description: NGC 5905 is a barred spiral galaxy in Draco about 150 million light-years away. It was the host of one of the first confirmed tidal disruption events, where a passing star was shredded by its central black hole and produced a powerful soft X-ray flare observed in 1990. Its bar and two main spiral arms are visible in moderate-depth imaging.

name: Splinter Galaxy
description: The Splinter Galaxy (or Knife Edge Galaxy) is an almost perfectly edge-on spiral in Draco about 50 million light-years away, whose razor-thin disk stretches nearly 13 arcminutes across the sky. A spectacular system of faint tidal stellar loops and streams encircles the galaxy, discovered in deep photographic surveys, and is thought to be the remains of a small satellite galaxy that was absorbed billions of years ago. Its extraordinarily flat profile makes it one of the most frequently depicted edge-on galaxies.

name: NGC 596
description: NGC 596 is an elliptical galaxy in the constellation Cetus. The galaxy lies 65 million light years away from Earth, which means, given its apparent dimensions, that NGC 596 is approximately 60,000 light years across.

name: NGC 5982
description: NGC 5982 is an elliptical galaxy located in the constellation Draco. It is located at a distance of about 130 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 5982 is about 100,000 light years across.

name: NGC 6118
description: NGC 6118 is a grand design spiral galaxy located 83 million light-years away in the constellation Serpens. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on 14 April 1785.

name: NGC 613
description: NGC 613 is a barred spiral galaxy located 67 million light years away in the southern constellation of Sculptor. The galaxy was discovered by German-English astronomer William Herschel on 9 December 1798, then re-discovered and catalogued by Scottish astronomer James Dunlop on 5 August 1826.

name: NGC 615
description: NGC 615 is an unbarred spiral galaxy seen edge-on located in the constellation Cetus. It is located at a distance of circa 70 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 615 is about 75,000 light years across.

name: NGC 6207
description: NGC 6207 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Hercules. It is designated as SA(s)c in the galaxy morphological classification scheme and was discovered by William Herschel on 16 May 1787.

name: Turtle Nebula
description: This object was first recorded as a star-like feature by Joseph Lalande on March 22, 1799. However, credit for the discovery of a nebula goes to Wilhelm Struve in 1825.

name: NGC 6229
description: NGC 6229 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Hercules. It is designated as GC(v)B in the galaxy morphological classification scheme and was discovered by the British astronomer William Herschel on 12 May 1787.

name: NGC 6231
description: NGC 6231 is one of the most luminous young open clusters in the Milky Way, lying about 5,900 light-years away in Scorpius and containing over 100 massive hot stars, including several O supergiants and Wolf-Rayet stars. Estimated at only 3 to 5 million years old, it is surrounded by extensive nebulosity and embedded in a rich association of young stars designated Scorpius OB1. Its brilliant stellar concentration is striking in binoculars and often called the Northern Jewel Box by analogy with NGC 4755 in Crux.

name: NGC 6235
description: NGC 6235 is a globular cluster in the constellation Ophiuchus, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 7.2, spanning about 4 arcminutes, it is an easy target for small telescopes.

name: NGC 6284
description: NGC 6284 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Ophiuchus. It is designated as IX in the galaxy morphological classification scheme and was discovered by the German-born British astronomer William Herschel on 22 May 1784.

name: NGC 6287
description: NGC 6287 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Ophiuchus. It is designated as VII in the galaxy morphological classification scheme and was discovered by the German-born British astronomer William Herschel on 21 May 1784.

name: NGC 6293
description: NGC 6293 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Ophiuchus. Its Shapley–Sawyer Concentration Class is IV.

name: Bug Nebula
description: The Bug Nebula (also called the Butterfly Nebula) is one of the most complex and extreme planetary nebulae known, about 3,800 light-years away in Scorpius. Its central star is one of the hottest white dwarfs ever observed at roughly 250,000 Kelvin, and it drives two enormous wing-like lobes of ionised gas extending over 2 light-years in length. Hubble images reveal intricate shock structures, jets, and a dusty equatorial torus in this rapidly evolving bipolar nebula.

name: NGC 6304
description: NGC 6304 is a globular cluster in the constellation Ophiuchus. William Herschel discovered this star cluster using an 18.5-inch (47 cm) f/13 speculum reflector telescope in 1786. It is about 19,000 light-years away, near the Milky Way's central bulge.

name: Box Nebula
description: NGC 6309, also known as the Box Nebula, is a planetary nebula located in the constellation Ophiuchus. It was discovered by the German astronomer Wilhelm Tempel in 1876.

name: NGC 6316
description: NGC 6316 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Ophiuchus. Its Shapley-Sawyer Concentration Class is III, meaning that it has a "strong inner core of stars" and was discovered by the German-born British astronomer William Herschel on 24 May 1784.

name: Cat's Paw Nebula
description: The Cat's Paw Nebula is a large, bright emission nebula in Scorpius about 5,500 light-years away, whose three main circular glowing regions suggest an enormous feline paw print. It is an intensely active star-forming region, estimated to have produced an unusually large number of stars in the past few million years, and Spitzer infrared observations have revealed hundreds of embedded young stellar objects invisible at optical wavelengths. It is a vivid red in narrowband photographs but requires dark southern skies to detect its faint outer extent visually.

name: NGC 6342
description: NGC 6342 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Ophiuchus. Its Shapley–Sawyer Concentration Class is IV, and it was discovered by the German-born British astronomer William Herschel on 28 May 1786. It is at a distance of 28,000 light years away from Earth.

name: NGC 6355
description: NGC 6355 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Ophiuchus. It is at a distance of 28,000 light years away from Earth, and is currently part of the Galactic bulge.

name: NGC 6356
description: NGC 6356 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Ophiuchus. It is designated as a II in the Shapley–Sawyer Concentration Class and was discovered by the German-born British astronomer William Herschel on 18 June 1784.

name: Lobster Nebula
description: The War and Peace Nebula is a complex emission nebula in Scorpius about 8,000 light-years away, containing several young open clusters embedded within a vast cloud of ionised gas. In Western orientation the west half suggests a dove of peace while the east half looks like a skull. One of its embedded clusters, Pismis 24, contains some of the most massive stars known, with several candidates exceeding 100 solar masses.

name: Little Ghost Nebula
description: Little Ghost Nebula, also known as NGC 6369, is a planetary nebula in the constellation Ophiuchus. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1784.

name: NGC 637
description: The cluster was discovered on 9 November 1787 by German-born English astronomer William Herschel. It is located in the Perseus Arm of the Milky Way, at a distance of approximately 7,045 light years from the Sun.

name: NGC 6388
description: NGC 6388 is one of the most massive and densely packed globular clusters in the Milky Way, lying about 36,900 light-years away in Scorpius. It is unusually metal-rich for such a massive cluster and harbors an unexpected mix of RR Lyrae variables, Cepheid-like variables, and blue straggler stars — stellar populations not expected to coexist at this metallicity. Unusually for a globular cluster, it displays a disk-like morphology in its outermost regions suggesting it has been substantially shaped by tidal forces.

name: NGC 6397
description: NGC 6397 is the second nearest globular cluster to Earth at only about 7,800 light-years in Ara, and because of this proximity it is one of the most deeply studied stellar systems in astronomy. Its stars are among the most thoroughly resolved of any globular, enabling Hubble observations to identify individual white dwarfs and measure precise stellar ages of around 13.4 billion years. Its core has undergone gravitational collapse, creating one of the highest central stellar densities of any cluster at this distance.

name: NGC 6401
description: NGC 6401 is a globular cluster in the equatorial constellation of Ophiuchus. This star cluster was discovered by German-English astronomer William Herschel in 1784, but he mistakenly classified it as a bright nebula.

name: NGC 6426
description: NGC 6426 is a globular cluster of stars located in the equatorial constellation of Ophiuchus. It was discovered by the German-English astronomer William Herschel on 3 June 1786.

name: NGC 6440
description: NGC 6440 is a globular cluster of stars in the southern constellation of Sagittarius. It was discovered by German-English astronomer William Herschel on 28 May 1786.

name: NGC 6441
description: NGC 6441 is a large, compact globular cluster in Scorpius about 38,500 light-years away, one of the most luminous and metal-rich globulars in the Milky Way and a close companion in the sky to NGC 6388. Like NGC 6388, it puzzlingly hosts long-period Cepheid-like variables and RR Lyrae stars in numbers far exceeding what standard stellar evolution predicts for its metallicity. Its very high central stellar density and massive helium-enhanced stellar population make it an important testbed for theories of globular cluster formation.

name: Box Nebula
description: NGC 6445, also known as the Little Gem Nebula or Box Nebula, is a planetary nebula in the constellation Sagittarius. It was discovered by William Herschel on May 28, 1786.

name: NGC 6451
description: NGC 6451 is an open cluster in the constellation Scorpius, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 8.2, spanning about 7 arcminutes, it is a modest target for amateur telescopes.

name: NGC 6517
description: NGC 6517 is a globular cluster in the constellation Ophiuchus, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 11.08, spanning about 5 arcminutes, it is a faint target best suited to larger telescopes or long-exposure imaging.

name: NGC 6522
description: NGC 6522 is a globular cluster of stars in the southern constellation of Sagittarius. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on June 24, 1784.

name: NGC 6528
description: NGC 6528 is a globular cluster in the constellation Sagittarius, and is listed in the New General Catalogue. It has an apparent magnitude of about 11 and a diameter of about 16 arcminutes, and its Shapley–Sawyer Concentration Class is V, containing stars of 16th magnitude and dimmer.

name: NGC 654
description: NGC 654 is an open cluster in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1787.

name: NGC 6540
description: NGC 6540 is a globular cluster of stars in the souther constellation Sagittarius, positioned about 4.66° away from the Galactic Center. It was discovered by German-British astronomer Wilhelm Herschel on May 24, 1784, with an 18.7-inch mirror telescope, who described the cluster a…

name: Cat's Eye Nebula
description: The Cat's Eye Nebula is a complex, intricate planetary nebula in Draco about 3,300 light-years away, and one of the most structurally elaborate planetary nebulae known. Concentric shells, jets, and knotty blobs surround a bright inner ellipse, all formed by a series of mass-loss episodes from the dying central star. It was the first nebula to have its chemical composition studied through spectroscopy, by William Huggins in 1864.

name: NGC 6544
description: NGC 6544 is a small globular cluster visible in the constellation Sagittarius. It is magnitude 7.5, diameter 1 arcminute. It is less than 1 degree southeast of Messier 8, the Lagoon Nebula.

name: NGC 6553
description: NGC 6553 is a globular cluster in the constellation Sagittarius. Its Shapley–Sawyer Concentration Class is XI, meaning the star concentration is very loose even at the center; it has stars of magnitude 20 and dimmer.

name: NGC 6559
description: NGC 6559 is an emission and reflection nebula in Sagittarius about 3,900 light-years away, lying just east of the Lagoon Nebula and connected to the same giant molecular cloud complex. It consists of a patchwork of red emission regions, blue reflection patches, and dark Bok globules, creating a colourful, varied texture in photographs. Though small in apparent size, its proximity to M8 and the richness of the surrounding star field make it a natural wide-field companion target.

name: NGC 6568
description: NGC 6568 is an open cluster in the constellation Sagittarius, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 8.6, spanning about 8 arcminutes, it is a modest target for amateur telescopes.

name: NGC 6569
description: NGC 6569 is a globular cluster in the constellation Sagittarius. It is about 2 degrees south east of Gamma2 Sagittarii.

name: NGC 6572
description: NGC 6572 is a planetary nebula in the constellation Ophiuchus. It was discovered in 1825 by the German astronomer Friedrich Georg Wilhelm von Struve.

name: NGC 6584
description: NGC 6584 is a globular cluster in the constellation Telescopium that lies near Theta Arae and is 45000 light-years distant.

name: NGC 659
description: NGC 659, also known as the Yin-Yang Cluster is an open cluster in the Cassiopeia constellation. It was discovered by Caroline Herschel in 1783.

name: NGC 660
description: NGC 660 is a peculiar and unique polar-ring galaxy located approximately 45 million light-years from Earth in the Pisces constellation. It is the only such galaxy having, as its host, a "late-type lenticular galaxy".

name: NGC 6604
description: NGC 6604 is an open cluster in Serpens, about 5,500 light-years away, embedded in faint emission nebulosity. It contains several hot O-type stars that are ionising the surrounding gas to produce the nebula Sh2-54. Its young age and hot stellar content make it an interesting object in the context of massive star formation in that region of the Milky Way.

name: NGC 6629
description: NGC 6629 is a planetary nebula in the constellation of Sagittarius, located above the "Teapot". The object formed when a star ejected its outer layers during the late stages of its evolution.

name: NGC 663
description: NGC 663 is a rich, bright open cluster in Cassiopeia about 6,850 light-years away, containing around 400 member stars of which several dozen are bright enough to be resolved in a moderate telescope. Several Be stars with emission-line spectra populate the cluster, and it lies in a dense Milky Way field that enhances the visual impression of richness. Its estimated age of around 20 to 25 million years makes it a very young cluster still dominated by hot blue-white supergiants.

name: NGC 6633
description: NGC 6633 is a large, bright open cluster in Ophiuchus about 1,040 light-years away, spanning over a degree of sky and best viewed in binoculars or a richfield telescope. It contains around 30 brighter members with an estimated age of 660 million years, making it a relatively old open cluster with several evolved yellow and orange giant stars. It lies close to the compact cluster IC 4756 for a rewarding wide-field comparison.

name: NGC 6638
description: NGC 6638 is a globular cluster in the constellation Sagittarius. It is magnitude 9.5 and diameter 2 arc minutes, class VI. It is a half degree east of Lambda Sagittarii. It is a member of the Milky Way.

name: NGC 6642
description: NGC 6642 is a globular cluster located 26,700 light-years from Earth, in the constellation Sagittarius. Many "blue stragglers" have been spotted in this globular, and it is known to be lacking in low-mass stars.

name: NGC 6645
description: NGC 6645 is an open cluster in the constellation Sagittarius, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 8.5, spanning about 5 arcminutes, it is a modest target for amateur telescopes.

name: NGC 6664
description: NGC 6664 is an open cluster in Scutum. It is located near NGC 6649.

name: NGC 6712
description: NGC 6712 is a globular cluster that was probably discovered by Le Gentil on July 9, 1749 when investigating the Milky Way star cloud in Aquila. He described it as a "true nebula," in contrast to the open star cluster M11.

name: NGC 6717
description: NGC 6717 is a globular cluster in the constellation Sagittarius, and is a member of the Palomar Globular Clusters group. Palomar 9 was discovered by William Herschel on August 7, 1784. It is located about 7,300 parsecs away from Earth.

name: NGC 6723
description: NGC 6723, also known as the Chandelier Cluster, is a globular cluster in the constellation Sagittarius. It is a class VII cluster with stars of magnitude 14 and dimmer.

name: Phantom Streak Nebula
description: NGC 6741, also known as the Phantom Streak Nebula, is located about 7000 light-years away in the constellation of Aquila.

name: NGC 6745
description: NGC 6745 is an irregular galaxy about 206 million light-years away in the constellation Lyra. It was discovered by French astronomer Édouard Stephan on 24 July 1879.

name: NGC 6752
description: NGC 6752 is the third brightest globular cluster in the sky and one of the most-studied, lying about 13,000 light-years away in Pavo. Its outer regions are unusually rich compared to most globulars and are easily resolved into individual stars even at the cluster's periphery. Studies of its white dwarf population provided one of the most precise age measurements for a globular cluster, pegging it at around 11.78 billion years old. It is a showpiece object for southern hemisphere observers.

name: NGC 6760
description: NGC 6760 is a globular cluster in the constellation Aquila. It may have contributed to the formation of the open cluster Ruprecht 127 during NGC 6760's passage through the galactic disk 71 million years ago.

name: NGC 6781
description: It was discovered July 30, 1788 by the Anglo-German astronomer William Herschel. The nebula lies at a distance of 1,500 ly from the Sun.

name: NGC 6790
description: NGC 6790 is a young, compact planetary nebula with a high surface brightness located in the equatorial constellation of Aquila. Imaging by the Hubble Space Telescope shows elongated shells surrounding the central star.

name: NGC 6802
description: NGC 6802 is an open cluster in the constellation Vulpecula, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 8.8, spanning about 5 arcminutes, it is a modest target for amateur telescopes.

name: Little Gem Nebula
description: The Little Gem Nebula or NGC 6818 is a planetary nebula located in the constellation of Sagittarius. It has magnitude 10 and oval diameter of 15 to 22 arcseconds with a 15th magnitude central star.

name: Barnard's Galaxy
description: Barnard's Galaxy is an isolated irregular dwarf galaxy and member of the Local Group, lying about 1.63 million light-years away in Sagittarius. Discovered by E. E. Barnard in 1884, it contains numerous bright HII star-forming regions and young stellar associations spread across an irregular disk roughly 7,000 light-years in diameter. Its proximity makes it a detailed laboratory for studying dwarf galaxy evolution, and several of its HII regions rival the Orion Nebula in physical size.

name: NGC 6823
description: NGC 6820 is a small emission nebula near the open cluster NGC 6823 in Vulpecula. The reflection nebula and cluster are embedded in a large faint emission nebula called Sh 2-86. The whole area of nebulosity is often referred to as NGC 6820.

name: NGC 6830
description: NGC 6830, also known as the Poodle Cluster, is an open cluster in Vulpecula. It contains about 150 members. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1784.

name: NGC 6834
description: NGC 6834 is a young open cluster of stars located about 10,850 light years from the Sun in the constellation Cygnus. It was discovered on July 17, 1784, by Anglo-German astronomer William Herschel.

name: NGC 6866
description: NGC 6866 is a young open cluster of stars in the northern constellation Cygnus. It was discovered by German astronomer Caroline Herschel on 23 July 1783.

name: Crescent Nebula
description: The Crescent Nebula is a wind-blown emission nebula in Cygnus about 5,000 light-years away, formed by the powerful stellar wind of the central Wolf-Rayet star WR 136 slamming into material previously shed during the star's red-giant phase. The resulting shell of ionised, compressed gas glows in vivid hydrogen-alpha and doubly ionised oxygen. It is one of the most popular narrowband astrophotography targets in the summer sky.

name: Blue Flash Nebula
description: NGC 6905, also known as the Blue Flash Nebula, is a planetary nebula in the constellation Delphinus. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1784.

name: NGC 6910
description: NGC 6910 is a compact open cluster in Cygnus about 3,700 light-years away, embedded in the extended emission nebulosity surrounding Gamma Cygni. Its two brightest members, a pair of blue and yellow supergiants, stand out visually, and the cluster contains around 20 confirmed members with an age of roughly 6 to 8 million years. In wide-field images it sits within the intricate Sadr region emission nebula.

name: NGC 6914
description: NGC 6914 is a striking pair of reflection nebulae in Cygnus about 6,000 light-years away, embedded within the diffuse emission region that fills the constellation. Two bright blue patches of reflected starlight from the embedded stellar association Cygnus OB2 float against a faint red hydrogen-alpha emission backdrop. The strong color contrast between the blue reflection cores and the surrounding red emission makes it a favourite colour photography target.

name: NGC 6939
description: NGC 6939 is an open cluster in the constellation Cepheus. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1798. The cluster lies 2/3° northwest from the spiral galaxy NGC 6946. The cluster lies approximately 4,000 light years away and it is over a billion years old.

name: NGC 6940
description: NGC 6940 is an open cluster in the constellation Vulpecula. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1784. The cluster is nearly a billion years old and it is located 2,500 light years away. It is considered the finest open cluster in the constellation.

name: Western Veil Nebula
description: NGC 6960 is the western filament of the Veil Nebula complex in Cygnus, the remnant of a supernova explosion that occurred roughly 10,000 to 20,000 years ago about 2,100 light-years away. The filament, sometimes called the Witch's Broom, drapes across the bright naked-eye star 52 Cygni which lies in the foreground. In narrowband images the delicate shock-excited wisps of hydrogen, oxygen, and sulfur glow in vivid, layered colours.

name: Eastern Veil Nebula
description: NGC 6992 is the bright eastern arc of the Veil Nebula supernova remnant in Cygnus, about 2,100 light-years away, and the most visually prominent section of the complex. Its gracefully curved shock front and extraordinary filamentary detail in long-exposure photographs make it one of the most admired emission nebulae in the sky. Together with NGC 6960 and the central Pickering's Triangle, it forms the complete Veil Nebula.

name: North America Nebula
description: The North America Nebula is a large emission nebula in Cygnus about 2,590 light-years away, whose outline unmistakably traces the shape of the North American continent, complete with the Gulf of Mexico. It spans about 100 light-years in its widest dimension and is ionised by a massive O-type star that lies in the obscuring dust just east of its bright region. In hydrogen-alpha photographs it is one of the most visually complex and detailed nebulae in the northern sky.

name: Fetus Nebula
description: NGC 7008, also known as the Fetus Nebula, is a planetary nebula with a diameter of approximately 1 light-year located at a distance of 2800 light years in northern Cygnus. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1787, in Slough, England.

name: Saturn Nebula
description: The Saturn Nebula is a bright planetary nebula in Aquarius about 5,000 light-years away, named by Lord Rosse for the pair of faint handle-like extensions (ansae) that give it a ringed appearance like the planet Saturn. These extensions are real jets of ionised gas produced by the central white dwarf, and a complete set of nested inner and outer shells makes it one of the most structurally detailed bright planetaries. Its vivid blue-green colour from doubly ionised oxygen is visible even in a small telescope.

name: Iris Nebula
description: The Iris Nebula is a bright, beautiful reflection nebula in Cepheus about 1,300 light-years away, surrounding the hot star SAO 19158. The illuminating star's blue light scatters off surrounding dust, giving the nebula a characteristic blue glow, while filaments of dark nebulosity lace through the surrounding molecular cloud. Deep images reveal a complex of filamentary dark nebulae extending well beyond the bright central reflection region.

name: NGC 7026
description: NGC 7026, also known as the Cheeseburger Nebula, is a planetary nebula located 6000 light-years away, in the constellation of Cygnus. The central star of the planetary nebula has a spectral type of [WO3], indicating a spectrum similar to that of an oxygen-rich Wolf–Rayet star.

name: Jewel Bug Nebula
description: NGC 7027 is one of the most luminous and youngest known planetary nebulae, located about 3,000 light-years away in Cygnus. It is extremely compact at only a few arcseconds across and is currently expanding rapidly from a central white dwarf. Radio and infrared observations make it one of the most thoroughly studied planetary nebulae, used as a standard calibration source for radio telescopes.

name: NGC 7044
description: NGC 7044 is an open cluster located in the Cygnus constellation. Containing approximately 742 stars, it was discovered by 18th century English astronomer William Herschel on 17 October 1786.

name: NGC 7062
description: NGC 7062 is an open cluster in the constellation Cygnus, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 8.3, spanning about 4 arcminutes, it is a modest target for amateur telescopes.

name: NGC 7086
description: NGC 7086 is an open cluster in the constellation Cygnus, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 8.4, spanning about 5 arcminutes, it is a modest target for amateur telescopes.

name: NGC 7128
description: NGC 7128 is an open cluster in the constellation Cygnus, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 9.7, spanning about 3 arcminutes, it is a modest target for amateur telescopes.

name: NGC 7129
description: NGC 7129 is a rose-tinted reflection nebula in Cepheus about 3,300 light-years away, illuminated by a cluster of young T Tauri and Herbig Ae/Be stars just a few million years old. Infrared observations have revealed numerous embedded young stellar objects, Herbig-Haro jets, and a molecular outflow invisible at optical wavelengths. Its pink-orange hue in photographs comes from a combination of blue reflection and faint hydrogen-alpha emission from shocked gas around the young stars.

name: NGC 7142
description: NGC 7142 is a rich but compact open cluster in Cepheus about 6,000 light-years away, estimated to be around 4 billion years old, making it one of the oldest known open clusters. Its great age means its original hot blue-white stars have long evolved away, leaving a relatively red, evolved stellar population. It lies adjacent to the reflection nebula NGC 7129 in the same rich Cepheus star-forming region.

name: NGC 7160
description: NGC 7160 is an open cluster in the constellation Cepheus. It was discovered by William Herschel on November 9, 1789.

name: NGC 7184
description: NGC 7184 is a barred spiral galaxy located in the constellation Aquarius. It is located at a distance of circa 100 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 7184 is about 236,000 light years across.

name: NGC 720
description: NGC 720 is an elliptical galaxy located in the constellation Cetus. It is located at a distance of about 80 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 720 is about 110,000 light years across.

name: NGC 7209
description: NGC 7209 is an open cluster in the constellation Lacerta. It was discovered by William Herschel on 19 October 1787.

name: NGC 7217
description: NGC 7217 is an unbarred spiral galaxy in the constellation Pegasus.

name: NGC 7261
description: NGC 7261 is an open cluster in the constellation Cepheus, part of the Herschel 400 observing list. At magnitude 8.4, spanning about 7 arcminutes, it is a modest target for amateur telescopes.

name: Helix Nebula
description: The Helix Nebula is the nearest planetary nebula to Earth at only 650 light-years in Aquarius, and the largest in apparent angular size at nearly 3 degrees across. Its complex multiple-shell structure includes thousands of dense cometary knots pointing away from the central white dwarf, shaped by the interaction of fast and slow stellar winds. Despite its enormous apparent size, its low surface brightness makes it invisible to the naked eye.

name: NGC 7331
description: NGC 7331 is a large unbarred spiral galaxy in Pegasus about 40 million light-years away, often described as a Milky Way analog. Its spiral arms are rich in star-forming regions and dust lanes, and it is surrounded by a group of background galaxies including the famous Stephan's Quintet just half a degree away. Its tilted disk reveals internal structure well, and it is one of the finest galaxy targets of the autumn sky.

name: Wizard Nebula
description: The Wizard Nebula is an emission nebula in Cepheus about 7,200 light-years away, surrounding the young open cluster NGC 7380. The cluster's hot O-type stars ionise the surrounding gas into a complex of glowing nebulosity, with dark columns and bright rims forming the wizard-like silhouette visible in narrowband photographs. It is a rich target for hydrogen-alpha imaging in the autumn sky.

name: NGC 7448
description: NGC 7448 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Pegasus. It is located at a distance of circa 80 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 7448 is about 60,000 light years across.

name: NGC 7510
description: NGC 7510 is an open cluster of stars located around 11,400 light years away in the constellation Cepheus, near the border with Cassiopeia. This cluster forms part of the Perseus Spiral Arm.

name: NGC 7538
description: NGC 7538 is a luminous emission nebula in Cepheus about 9,100 light-years away and one of the largest massive star-forming regions in the outer Milky Way. It contains several regions of intense new star formation, including one of the largest known protostellar objects, a collapsing massive gas core roughly 300 solar masses in content. In narrowband photographs it glows with complex hydrogen-alpha and oxygen emission around embedded hot young stars.

name: NGC 7606
description: NGC 7606 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Aquarius. It is located at a distance of about 100 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 7606 is about 200,000 light years across.

name: NGC 7619
description: NGC 7619 is an elliptical galaxy located in the constellation Pegasus. NGC 7619 and NGC 7626 are the dominant and brightest members of the Pegasus galaxy cluster. Both of them were discovered by William Herschel on September 26, 1785.

name: NGC 7626
description: NGC 7626 is an elliptical galaxy located in the constellation Pegasus. It was discovered on September 26, 1785, by the German-British astronomer William Herschel.

name: Bubble Nebula
description: The Bubble Nebula is a striking wind-blown emission nebula in Cassiopeia about 7,100 light-years away, formed by an intense stellar wind from the luminous O-type star BD+60 2522 carving a near-perfect sphere into the surrounding molecular cloud. The star that forms the bubble is 45 times the mass of the Sun and is offset from the centre of the bubble because the surrounding gas is denser on one side. Hubble images have made it one of the most iconic and recognisable nebulae in modern astronomy.

name: NGC 7686
description: NGC 7686 is a moderately-sized open cluster in the constellation Andromeda, containing about 80 stars. At magnitude 5.6, it is an easy target for binoculars and small telescopes.

name: NGC 772
description: NGC 772 is a large unbarred spiral galaxy approximately 106 million light-years away in the constellation Aries. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on 29 November 1785.

name: NGC 7723
description: NGC 7723 is a barred spiral galaxy located in the constellation Aquarius. It is located at a distance of about 90 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 7723 is about 95,000 light years across.

name: NGC 7727
description: NGC 7727 is a peculiar galaxy in the constellation Aquarius. It harbors two galactic nuclei, each containing a supermassive black hole, separated 1,600 light years apart. It was discovered by German-British astronomer William Herschel on 27 November 1785.

name: Caroline's Rose
description: Caroline's Rose Cluster is a rich, spectacular open cluster in Cassiopeia about 7,600 light-years away, discovered by Caroline Herschel in 1783 and containing around 600 confirmed members. Its elaborate chains and loops of stars create a rose or pinwheel pattern that rewards extended viewing at medium magnification. At roughly 1.6 billion years old it is one of the older open clusters, its evolved red giant members scattered among the fainter blue-white stars.

name: NGC 779
description: NGC 779 is a spiral galaxy seen edge-on, located in the constellation Cetus. It is located at a distance of circa 60 million light years from Earth, which, given its apparent dimensions, means that NGC 779 is about 70,000 light years across.

name: NGC 7793
description: NGC 7793 is a flocculent spiral galaxy in the southern constellation of Sculptor. It was discovered on July 14, 1826, by Scottish astronomer James Dunlop.

name: Little Sombrero Galaxy
description: NGC 7814, the Little Sombrero, is a nearly edge-on spiral galaxy in Pegasus about 40 million light-years away, resembling a smaller version of the famous Sombrero Galaxy (M104). A prominent dust lane runs along its equatorial plane, cutting through a substantial central bulge. Its edge-on geometry and dust lane make it a favourite comparison object alongside M104 for photographers exploring galactic morphology.

name: Cosmic Question Mark
description: NGC 7822 is a large emission nebula complex in Cepheus about 3,000 light-years away, one of the northernmost star-forming regions in the sky. Its brightest section features dramatic pillars of molecular gas sculpted by the ultraviolet radiation of the young hot star cluster BD+66 1673, whose most massive members are among the youngest O-type stars known. It is a vivid narrowband imaging target, glowing in layered hydrogen-alpha, oxygen, and sulfur emission.

name: Double Cluster (h Per)
description: NGC 869 is the western component of the famous Double Cluster in Perseus, a pair of young open clusters lying about 7,500 light-years from Earth. Together with NGC 884, it forms one of the finest naked-eye and binocular objects in the sky, a pair of rich glittering star fields easily resolved in any instrument. At roughly 5.6 million years old, NGC 869 is slightly younger than its companion NGC 884 and contains numerous luminous blue supergiant stars.

name: Double Cluster (χ Per)
description: NGC 884 is the eastern member of the Double Cluster in Perseus, about 7,600 light-years away and slightly older than its companion NGC 869 at around 6.4 million years. Its membership includes a distinctive population of red and orange supergiant stars, providing a warm color contrast to the predominantly blue members of NGC 869 in the same field. Together, the Double Cluster is one of the showpieces of the autumn sky.

name: Silver Sliver Galaxy
description: NGC 891 is a classic edge-on spiral galaxy in Andromeda, about 27.3 million light-years away, often used as a visual archetype for edge-on disk galaxies. A striking dark dust lane runs perfectly along its equatorial plane, dividing the galaxy's bright bulge into two symmetrical halves. It has been extensively studied for its extraplanar dust and its vertical structure, which probes how disk galaxies cycle gas and energy between the disk and halo.

name: NGC 908
description: NGC 908 is an unbarred spiral galaxy in the constellation Cetus. It was discovered on 20 September 1786 by William Herschel. This galaxy is 56 million light years away from Earth. It is the main galaxy in the NGC 908 group, which also includes NGC 899, NGC 907, and IC 223.

name: NGC 925
description: NGC 925 is a barred spiral galaxy in Triangulum about 30 million light-years away, notable for its loosely wound, asymmetric spiral arms and an off-center bar structure. It is a member of the NGC 1023 Group and was used as one of the key Cepheid calibration galaxies in the Hubble Space Telescope Key Project to measure the Hubble Constant. Its large apparent size and low surface brightness make it a photographic rather than a visual target.

name: NGC 936
description: NGC 936 is a barred lenticular galaxy in the constellation Cetus. It is at a distance of about 60 million light-years away from Earth.

name: NGC 957
description: NGC 957 is a loosely bound open cluster located in the constellation Perseus. It has an apparent magnitude of 7.6 and an approximate size of 11 arc-minutes. It is young at less than 11 million years old.

name: Tulip Nebula
description: Sharpless 101 (Sh 2-101) is a H II region emission nebula located in the constellation Cygnus. It is sometimes also called the Tulip Nebula because it appears to resemble the outline of a tulip when imaged photographically.

name: Little Butterfly Nebula
description: Sh2-100, nicknamed the Little Butterfly Nebula, is a small, bright emission nebula in Cygnus a few degrees south of Sadr, within the larger Cygnus X star-forming complex. Two lobes of ionized hydrogen gas either side of its central star give it a wing-like, butterfly silhouette in narrowband images. It is sometimes confused with NGC 6302, the Butterfly Nebula (also called the Bug Nebula) in Scorpius, an unrelated planetary nebula.

name: Barnard's Loop
description: Barnard's Loop is a giant arc of ionized hydrogen roughly 300 light-years across, sweeping through much of the Orion constellation and enclosing the Orion Nebula, Horsehead and Flame Nebula region within its curve. Its origin is debated: it may be the shell of an ancient supernova, or gas ionized and pushed outward by the hot young stars of the Orion OB1 association. A popular but demanding wide-field Hα target, since capturing its full extent needs a short focal length.

name: Medusa Nebula
description: The Medusa Nebula (also catalogued as Abell 21) is one of the largest and faintest planetary nebulae known, an old, expanding shell of gas shed by a dying sun-like star. Its wispy, filamentary arcs are said to resemble the snake hair of the Gorgon Medusa in long-exposure images.

name: Celestial Snow Angel
description: Sh2-106 is a compact star-forming region in Cygnus surrounding a massive young protostar, its hourglass-shaped lobes of blue reflection nebulosity and red ionized hydrogen resembling a snow angel, a resemblance popularized by a well-known Hubble image. A ring of dust and gas around the central star's equator pinches the outflow into its distinctive bipolar shape.

name: Flying Bat Nebula
description: A faint emission nebula in Cepheus that surrounds the rare Squid Nebula (Ou4), a bipolar planetary-scale outflow only visible in OIII.

name: Cave Nebula
description: The Cave Nebula (Sh2-155) is an emission and reflection nebula complex in Cepheus about 2,400 light-years away, embedded within a large molecular cloud. The cave-shaped structure visible in hydrogen-alpha images is a blister of ionized gas on the edge of a dense dark cloud, illuminated and sculpted by the hot stars of the young cluster Cep OB3. Long-exposure narrowband images reveal a richly detailed landscape of glowing gas and dark obscuring pillars.

name: Spaghetti Nebula
description: It was discovered in 1952 at the Crimean Astrophysical Observatory by Grigory Shajn and his team using a Schmidt camera and a narrowband filter close to the Hydrogen Alpha transmission line. It is difficult to observe due to its extremely low surface brightness.

name: Flying Dragon Nebula
description: Sh2-114 is a faint emission nebula in southern Cygnus, nicknamed the Flying Dragon Nebula for the winding chain of glowing filaments that runs across it. It has a low surface brightness and is best recorded with hydrogen-alpha and narrowband filters over long exposures.

name: Lion Nebula
description: Sh2-132 is a large, faint emission nebula on the border of Cepheus and Lacerta, called the Lion Nebula for the crouching shape its brighter filaments form in narrowband images. It is energised by several hot massive stars, including two Wolf-Rayet stars, and lies roughly 10,000 light-years away in the Perseus arm.

name: Lobster Claw Nebula
description: Sh2-157 is an emission nebula in Cassiopeia, the Lobster Claw Nebula, named for the pair of curved ridges of glowing hydrogen that open like a claw. A compact young cluster and a Wolf-Rayet star drive its shells and bubbles. It lies near the Bubble Nebula and NGC 7635 in the sky, about 8,000 light-years away.

name: Dolphin Head Nebula
description: Sh2-308 is a large, nearly spherical emission nebula in Canis Major, the Dolphin Head Nebula, blown by the fierce wind of the hot Wolf-Rayet star EZ Canis Majoris at its centre. It glows mostly in the blue-green light of doubly ionized oxygen, giving it a bubble-like look. It lies roughly 5,200 light-years away.

name: NGC300
description: NGC 300 is a face-on spiral galaxy in Sculptor about 6.1 million light-years away, a member of the Sculptor Group and one of the nearest spiral galaxies to our Local Group. Its low surface brightness and wide apparent size make it a challenging visual object but a stunning photographic target, with delicate blue star-forming arms stretching across a large apparent diameter. Several Cepheid variable stars in NGC 300 have been used to calibrate the extragalactic distance scale.

name: Perseus A
description: NGC 1275 (Perseus A) is the central galaxy of the Perseus Galaxy Cluster, about 237 million light-years away, and one of the most powerful radio and X-ray sources in the sky. Its active galactic nucleus drives enormous bubbles of hot plasma into the surrounding intracluster medium, and Chandra X-ray Observatory images show these bubbles rippling sound waves through the cluster gas at the lowest frequency ever detected. Unusually thin filaments of cool gas extend thousands of light-years from the galaxy, dragged outward by rising plasma bubbles.

name: Fornax A
description: NGC 1316 (Fornax A) is the dominant galaxy of the Fornax Cluster, about 62 million light-years away and one of the most powerful radio sources in the sky. Extensive loops and shells in its outer envelope reveal a history of major galaxy mergers over the past billion years. It is the source of the most precisely measured extragalactic distance using Type Ia supernovae, making it a cornerstone of the cosmic distance ladder.

name: NGC1333
description: NGC 1333 is a reflection and emission nebula in Perseus, about 960 light-years away, embedded within one of the most active star-forming regions in the solar neighbourhood. Spitzer and Herschel infrared observations have revealed dozens of very young protostars and Herbig-Haro outflow jets hidden within its dense dust clouds. Visually it appears as a small blue reflection patch, but in infrared imagery it is a dynamic stellar nursery.

name: NGC1387
description: NGC 1387 is a lenticular galaxy in the Fornax Cluster, about 60 million light-years away, lying close in projection to the giant elliptical NGC 1399 at the cluster's center. Its smooth, featureless disk and bright nucleus are typical of lenticular cluster galaxies that have had their gas stripped by the intracluster medium. It is a common target in wide-field Fornax Cluster images.

name: NGC1399
description: NGC 1399 is the central giant elliptical galaxy of the Fornax Cluster, about 65 million light-years away, and one of the nearest dominant cluster ellipticals to Earth. It hosts an extraordinarily rich system of globular clusters, estimated at 5,700 total, some of which are being exchanged with the nearby galaxy NGC 1404 through tidal interactions. Its smooth, very round optical profile and powerful X-ray halo of hot gas are signatures of a classic cD-class cluster galaxy.

name: NGC1514
description: The Crystal Ball Nebula is a planetary nebula in Taurus about 1,500 light-years away, notable for its central binary star system consisting of a white dwarf and a giant companion. This binary is unusual in that the companion is still on the giant branch, providing clues to the timing of mass loss that created the nebula. Its hazy spherical appearance in moderate apertures gives it a bubble-like visual impression.

name: Hind's Nebula
description: Hind's Variable Nebula is a small reflection nebula in Taurus associated with the young T Tauri star T Tauri, about 460 light-years away. Its brightness fluctuates on timescales of months to years as clouds of dust between the illuminating star and the nebula shift and vary. T Tauri itself is the prototype of an entire class of young, pre-main-sequence variable stars.

name: NGC1624
description: NGC 1624 is an open cluster embedded in a faint emission nebula in Perseus, about 20,000 light-years away. The ionising source of the surrounding nebula is one of the most highly magnetised O-type stars known, making it an important object for studying stellar magnetic fields. The combination of cluster and nebula makes it a rewarding narrowband target.

name: NGC1672
description: NGC 1672 is a well-studied barred spiral galaxy in Dorado about 60 million light-years away, featuring an elongated nuclear bar surrounded by a star-forming ring and two broad outer spiral arms. It hosts a mildly active Seyfert 2 nucleus and numerous bright star-forming complexes along its bar and ring. Hubble Space Telescope imagery has made it one of the most visually detailed barred spirals studied at this distance.

name: NGC1805
description: NGC 1805 is a young open cluster in the Large Magellanic Cloud in the Dorado constellation, about 160,000 light-years away. It contains numerous hot massive stars and sits in a region of active star formation near the Tarantula Nebula complex. Its stars are only a few million years old, making it one of the youngest clusters in the LMC.

name: NGC1818
description: NGC 1818 is a young blue globular cluster in the Large Magellanic Cloud about 160,000 light-years away. With an age of only about 25 million years it is one of the youngest objects classified as a globular cluster, providing a rare opportunity to study the early stages of globular cluster evolution. Hubble observations have revealed an unusual blue straggler population given its youth, challenging models of how these stars form.

name: 30 Dor Cluster
description: The Tarantula Nebula is the most massive and luminous star-forming region in the Local Group of galaxies, located in the Large Magellanic Cloud about 160,000 light-years away. If placed at the distance of the Orion Nebula it would span 60 degrees of sky and cast visible shadows. At its heart is R136, a compact cluster containing several of the most massive stars known, each exceeding 100 solar masses.

name: NGC2175
description: NGC 2175 is the open cluster associated with and embedded within the Monkey Head Nebula (NGC 2174) in Orion. The cluster contains several O-type stars whose powerful radiation ionises and sculpts the surrounding cloud material. Though often listed separately, NGC 2174 and NGC 2175 together form the complete Monkey Head complex.

name: NGC2282
description: NGC 2282 is a faint reflection nebula in Monoceros, about 5,000 light-years away, surrounding a loose group of young stellar objects. It is one of several reflection patches in the rich Monoceros star-forming complex. Its relatively faint surface brightness requires dark skies and sensitive cameras to capture well.

name: NGC2327
description: NGC 2327 is a bright-rimmed emission and reflection nebula in Monoceros within the larger Seagull Nebula complex, about 3,800 light-years away. A bright-rimmed cloud on the leading edge of the Seagull's wing, it is being ionised and sculpted by the hot star HD 53623 embedded within. It is a vivid, compact target for narrowband imaging, particularly in hydrogen-alpha.

name: NGC2336
description: NGC 2336 is a large face-on barred spiral galaxy in Camelopardalis about 100 million light-years away, one of the most striking barred spirals in the northern sky despite its declination far from the galactic plane. Its well-defined bar, inner ring, and multiple spiral arms give it a complex and beautiful structure in photographs. Two supernovae have been recorded in its disk.

name: NGC2403
description: NGC 2403 is a spiral galaxy in Camelopardalis about 10 million light-years away, a member of the M81 Group and one of the nearest spiral galaxies visible from northern latitudes. Its face-on orientation and large apparent size reveal numerous HII star-forming regions scattered through its loosely wound arms, giving it a mottled, patchy appearance similar to M33. Hubble Cepheid measurements of this galaxy were key to early calibrations of the extragalactic distance scale.

name: Helix Galaxy
description: NGC 2685, the Helix Galaxy, is a rare polar ring galaxy in Ursa Major about 42 million light-years away. A ring of gas, dust, and stars orbits the main lenticular galaxy at nearly a right angle, forming the distinctive helix or polar ring visible in photographs. This unusual geometry is thought to have formed from a past interaction or merger with a gas-rich companion.

name: Spindle Galaxy
description: The Spindle Galaxy in Leo is a lenticular galaxy about 32 million light-years away, seen almost perfectly edge-on. It has one of the highest mass-to-light ratios measured in the local universe, indicating a dense dark matter halo and a supermassive central black hole of around one billion solar masses. Its razor-thin disk cutting through a large ellipsoidal bulge makes it one of the most geometrically striking galaxies in the sky.

name: NGC3190
description: NGC 3190 is a nearly edge-on spiral galaxy in Leo about 80 million light-years away and a prominent member of the Hickson Compact Group 44. Its tightly wound spiral arms and prominent dust lane make it visually striking, and gravitational interactions with its compact group neighbours are distorting its disk. Together with NGC 3193, NGC 3187, and NGC 3185 it forms one of the more accessible compact galaxy groups for amateur imagers.

name: NGC3718
description: NGC 3718 is a heavily distorted lenticular or spiral galaxy in Ursa Major about 52 million light-years away, classified as peculiar for its dramatically warped disk and prominent dark dust lane that curves right across the nucleus. A chain of five background galaxies called Arp 322 lies roughly 8 arcminutes to the south, providing a striking depth contrast in the same field. The warping is attributed to tidal interaction with its nearby companion NGC 3729.

name: Antennae Galaxies
description: NGC 4038, the northern Antennae Galaxy, is one half of a spectacular pair of colliding spiral galaxies in Corvus about 45 million light-years away. The collision has triggered a violent starburst producing thousands of young star clusters, concentrated in a luminous central overlap region that is one of the most intense star-forming sites in the local universe. The two galaxies are named for the long tidal tails that extend from the system like insect antennae.

name: Antennae Galaxies
description: NGC 4039 is the southern component of the Antennae Galaxies, a merging pair of spiral galaxies in Corvus about 45 million light-years away. Together with NGC 4038, it is one of the most-studied galaxy mergers in astronomy, providing a template for how larger collisions produce starburst activity and redistribute dark matter. The pair's long tidal tails and central starburst region are accessible to amateur telescopes from dark sites.

name: NGC4217
description: NGC 4217 is a nearly edge-on barred spiral galaxy in Canes Venatici about 60 million light-years away. Deep images reveal a spectacular extra-planar filamentary halo of ionised hydrogen gas extending far above and below the disk, thought to be driven outward by supernova-driven galactic winds. Its thin disk and faint outer halo make it a popular target for researchers studying feedback between disk star formation and the galactic halo.

name: NGC4244
description: The Silver Needle Galaxy is a perfectly edge-on spiral galaxy in Canes Venatici about 13.5 million light-years away, one of the flattest and most symmetric edge-on galaxies in the sky. Its thin, elongated disk stretches 65,000 light-years end to end with very little central bulge, making it appear as a simple luminous needle. It is one of the most photogenic edge-on galaxies for wide-field astrophotography.

name: NGC4449
description: NGC 4449 is a Magellanic irregular galaxy in Canes Venatici about 12 million light-years away, sometimes called the Box Galaxy for its roughly rectangular outline in small telescopes. It is one of the nearest starburst irregular galaxies, forming stars at a rate comparable to the Large Magellanic Cloud and full of luminous blue star clusters and HII regions. A long tidal stellar stream wraps around it, evidence of a past disruption of a smaller companion.

name: NGC4559
description: NGC 4559 is a barred spiral galaxy in Coma Berenices about 30 million light-years away, displaying loosely wound, patchy spiral arms rich in star-forming regions. An extremely luminous X-ray source in its disk has been identified as either a very massive X-ray binary or an intermediate-mass black hole. Its inclined disk reveals internal structure readily in photographs.

name: Whale Galaxy
description: The Whale Galaxy is an edge-on barred irregular galaxy in Canes Venatici about 25 million light-years away, whose tapered shape with a slightly bowed profile suggests a cetacean in profile. A spectacular corona of hot X-ray emitting gas surrounds its disk, driven aloft by dozens of supernova explosions. Its companion galaxy NGC 4627, a small elliptical, is visible just north of the Whale's spine in most telescope views.

name: NGC4727
description: NGC 4727 is a faint background galaxy in Coma Berenices, sometimes visible in the same telescope field as the more prominent NGC 4725 nearby. It is a distant member of the Coma-Virgo supercluster. It is a faint, generic-appearing elliptical or lenticular galaxy best captured in deep photographic exposures.

name: NGC5005
description: NGC 5005 is an inclined barred spiral galaxy in Canes Venatici about 65 million light-years away. Its warm, orange-tinted nuclear region and outer spiral arms make it a visually attractive and frequently imaged galaxy. It forms a wide physical pair with NGC 5033 about 45 arcminutes to the southeast.

name: NGC5248
description: NGC 5248 is a face-on barred spiral galaxy in Bootes about 59 million light-years away, famous for its tightly wound nuclear spiral visible in Hubble images. It has two sets of spiral arms at different scales, an inner ring of star formation and a broader outer spiral, giving it a layered complexity in photographs. It is one of the more photogenic face-on spirals for moderate-aperture imaging in the spring sky.

name: NGC5371
description: NGC 5371 is a grand design barred spiral galaxy in Canes Venatici about 98 million light-years away, one of the most prominent spiral galaxies in that constellation.
